Catholic life and Mission
St Aidan's is a Catholic Primary School where we serve the Catholic community of Seven Kings. We welcome children and staff of all faiths where we celebrate and learn from one another. We follow our mission statement of 'Together we enjoy Learning, Achieving, sharing and praying. Let Jesus' love shine through in everything we do.'
We gather together for prayer and liturgy as a whole school, class groups and phase groups to share the word of God and sing together. When we pray we are lifting up our hearts and minds to God, we do this through many ways of prayer. Christ is at the centre of all we do and strive for at St Aidan's.
For the teaching of Religious Education we follow the new RED (Religious Education Directory)

Pope Francis has written a letter addressed to every person on the planet asking us all to protect the earth.
Watch this animation - Click on the image
The earth is God's gift to us all, full of beauty and wonder. And it belongs to everyone. But what we see today is that our common home has never been so hurt and mistreated. We have developed at a greater speed that we never could have imagined, and have treated the earth like it has an unlimited supply of resources. We have taken more than our fair share from most people on the planet, as well as future generations. We have cut down the earths natural forests, polluted the earths waters, it's land and it's air.
The whole human family needs to work together to care for our planet earth, so that we sow beauty not pollution and destruction. So let's put pure love for the world and love for our neighbours, into action by living together in harmony and caring for nature.
-Will you play your part to look after our common home?
-Can you take simple every day eco-actions to care for the earth, like turning off lights or reducing water waste?
-And will you live more simply, reducing the amount of things we buy and throw away?
The world can't wait so let's make that start today! Play your part to protect our common home.
Religious Education is central to the life of St Aidan's. It promotes the spiritual, moral, cultural, mental and physical development of the pupils and enables them to become aware of God's presence in their lives, helping them to foster a caring Christian attitude towards others. RE also enables pupils to gain knowledge and understanding of the major world faiths, while recognising the many similarities and differences which link faiths together.
Our RE programme, RED, is based on upon the core resources recommended by the diocese. Each year group from Yr 1-6 have their own list of focus topics to consider throughout the academic year. The topic will coincide with the church calendar. At the heart of the programme is the mystery of God's self-revelation of love through Jesus Christ. RED gives our pupils the opportunity to explore the mystery of faith through Scripture and tradition.

About Us
A Welcome from our headteacher
Welcome to St Aidan’s,
I am extremely proud to lead a strong Catholic school community who are on a rapid journey of improvement all striving for excellence. I began my teaching career at St Aidan’s as an NQT many years ago and now feel blessed to return to lead the school on its successful pathway.
Our school mission statemeant: ‘Together we enjoy learning, achieving, sharing and praying. Let Jesus’ love shine through in everything we do’ is at the heart of all we do here at St Aidan’s. Every child is provided with the opportunity to shine and achieve. We strive to ensure that every child is happy and safe so they can thrive and enjoy learning. At St Aidan’s our pupils wear their uniform with pride and are excited to come to school each day!
St Aidan’s Catholic Primary Academy is part of the Good Shepherd Catholic Trust, a Multi Academy Trust of 8 Catholic schools in the Diocese of Brentwood. We work collaboratively with the MAT all striving for excellent Catholic education for all our pupils.
The community is stronger than ever and the children are kind, hardworking and positive. The journey of school improvement is equally challenging, rewarding and exciting for everyone concerned.
I am delighted to be part of this process to offer our pupils the best opportunities in life. The Governing Body and I thank you all for your continuous commitment and support on our journey.

Values
St Aidan's Catholic Values and Ethos
Gospel Values are what Jesus said, what Jesus did and what He told us to do.
All of the Gospel Values begin with and derive from Jesus' Law of Love:Respect for the Life and Dignity of Each Individual.
'Together we enjoy learning, achieving, sharing and praying. Let Jesus' love shine through in everything we do.'
The DfE have reinforced the need ''to create and enforce a clear and rigorous expectation on all schools to promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.''
The government set out its definition of British values in the 2011 Prevent Strategy, and these values have been reiterated by the Prime Minister this year.
At St Aidan's Catholic Primary Academy these values are reinforced regularly and in the following ways.
We seek to ensure that all pupils experience and gain an understanding of Democracy through concrete learning opportunities. For example we have an established pupil voice in School through our House Forum meetings. Every fortnight pupils are consulted as to their views and opinions through our House Forum meetings and also regularly through individual questionnaires. One example of listening to and acting on the views of pupil voice was the introduction of fundraising for their chosen charity.
The importance of Laws, whether they be those that govern the class, the school, or the country, are consistently reinforced throughout regular school days, as well as when dealing with behaviour and through school assemblies. Pupils are taught the value and reasons behind laws, that they govern and protect us, the responsibilities that this involves and the consequences when laws are broken.
Within our school pupils are actively encouraged to make choices, knowing that they are in a safe and supportive environment. As a school we educate and provide boundaries for young pupils to make choices safely, through the provision of a safe environment and empowering education. Pupils are encouraged to know, understand and exercise their rights and personal freedoms and advise how to exercise these safely, for example through our E-Safety and PSHE lessons. Whether it be through choice or challenge, of how they record, of participation in our numerous extra-curricular clubs and opportunities, pupils are given the freedom to make choices.
As a school community we take the obligation of mutual respect for others as the cultural richness of our school and wider community seriously. As a Catholic school we place 'Christ at the Centre' of what we seek as a school and the highest priority in this work is to ensure that all pupils, cultures and faiths are recognised and respected within our school family. Our school ethos and Good Behaviour Policy takes the core value of 'Respect' as a key starting point. Throughout the school year teachers and adults model this key value and discuss topics of respect through our class discussions and school assembly. Wall displays throughout the school emphasise the key aspects of what we believe and conversations with the pupils confirm their understanding of Mutual Respect.
Tolerance of those of Different Faiths and Beliefs
An integral part of the Catholic tradition is that of encompassing other faith beliefs as a Catholic School community. This is achieved through enchancing pupils understanding of their place in a culturally diverse society and by giving them opportunities to experience such diversity. Assemblies and discussions involving prejudices and prejudice-based bullying have been followed and supported by learning in RE and PSHE. Members of different faiths or religions are encouraged to share their knowledge to enhance learning within classes and the school

I am very happy for everything and appreciate all the support especially the teachers who take their time to teach my daughter. Thank you very much to the school, teachers and Headteacher I really appreciate your support.
During the lockdown period it was unprecedented times for all the children but the school made our son feel safe and happy. He makes good progress and the school communicate really well with us about how well he is doing.
It has been a huge strength to see the school have the ability to make changes and improvements. Over the past 2 years there have been tremendous improvments for the better. I am so happy to have my children come to the school they are happy and thriving.
The school has good discipline and values throughout which a great sense of community and belonging. Thank you for how well you communicate with us for what is going on.
I really appreciate my sons hardwork during his learning and i want to pay my gratitude to the school for teaching him the right attitude, I know under your guidance he will excel.

Curriculum
Staff and governors at St Aidan’s Catholic Primary Academy believe the development of pupils, spiritually, morally and socially plays a significant part in their ability to learn and achieve. We aim to provide an education that provides children with opportunities to explore and develop their own values and beliefs, spiritual awareness, high standards of behaviour, a positive caring attitude towards others and an appreciation of the diversity of our school. This is embedded throughout all aspects of school life through the use of our values such as love, respect, unity, friendship, honesty, kindness, tolerance, patience, appreciation, courage, trust and understanding.
Our Curriculum
• Where our strong Catholic ethos permeates through life, providing the children with a safe, calm and nurturing environment.
• That has knowledge and vocabulary at the heart of their learning.• That is rich and enables children to see the world from a range of different perspectives.• Where knowledge underpins and enables the application of skills.• Where the needs of all children are catered for• Where we have clear and consistent methods for celebrating success• That offers opportunities to delve deeper into their learning through progression of skills.• That equips children with the knowledge of how to live healthy lifestyles – both physically and mentally. • That promotes and reflects British Values.• Where spiritual, moral and social are interwoven in all that we do.• That enables children to connect to the past, live in the present and look to the future

SEND & INCLUSION
Inclusion:
At St Aidan's we are committed to creating an inclusive, welcoming and supportive environment where every child is valued, respected and given the opportunity to thrive.
Our approach:
Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND)
We are committed to ensuring that pupils with special educational needs and disabilities receive the appropriate support to make progress and develop their confidence and independence.
Our staff work collaboratively to understand each child's individual needs and put appropriate strategies and support in place. We regularly review provision and progress so that support can be adapted as children develop.
Our Inclusion Lead - Miss Williamson
If you would like to discuss your child’s additional needs, SEND provision or the support they are currently receiving, please do not hesitate to get in touch with our Inclusion Lead, Miss Williamson. We value working closely with families to ensure that children receive the support they need to thrive.
You can request a call from Miss Williamson using the form below. She will aim to return your call within 5 working days. Please briefly outline the reason for your call so that she can best support you. If you feel your query requires more immediate attention, please provide details on the form or contact the school office directly.
Alternatively, you can contact us by:
Email: [email protected]
Telephone: 020 8590 5223
Working with families:
We believe that strong relationships with families are essential to successful inclusion. We welcome open communication with parents and carers and encourage families to speak to us if they have concerns, questions or information they feel would help us to better support their child.
Our aim is for every child to feel safe, included, confident and ready to learn.
If you would like to discuss your child's needs or find out more about our approach to inclusion, please contact Miss Williamson.
Identifying and Supporting Additional Needs
At St Aidan’s, we recognise that children’s needs may emerge or change at different points during their school journey. Additional needs may be identified through ongoing assessment, observations, discussions with families, pupil voice, progress over time or information shared by other professionals.
We follow a graduated approach to supporting pupils with SEND through a cycle of Assess, Plan, Do and Review. This enables us to understand each child’s strengths and barriers to learning, put appropriate support in place and regularly review its impact.
Support is adapted in response to each child’s progress and individual needs. Where appropriate, we work in partnership with families and seek advice from external professionals to further understand and support a child’s needs.
Inclusive Teaching and Adaptive Practice
At St Aidan’s, inclusion begins in the classroom. Our curriculum is designed to meet the needs of the children in our school and to ensure that all pupils have access to ambitious and meaningful learning.
Teachers plan with adaptive teaching at the heart of their practice. Rather than creating a separate curriculum for pupils with SEND, teaching is adapted to remove barriers and enable children to access learning alongside their peers wherever possible.
We use the EEF Five-a-Day approach to support high-quality teaching for pupils with SEND. This includes:
· Explicit instruction
· Cognitive and metacognitive strategies
Where a child requires additional support beyond inclusive classroom teaching, targeted interventions or specialist provision may be introduced and reviewed as part of the graduated approach.
*an example of a really strong adaptive teaching template to show how work is adapted…
For further information about what we teach and how learning is sequenced across the school, please visit our Curriculum page.
Teachers use their knowledge of each child, alongside assessment and individual support plans, to select appropriate adaptations. These may include changes to resources, communication, task presentation, adult support, the learning environment or the way children demonstrate their understanding.
Individual Education Plans (IEPs)
At St Aidan’s, children receiving SEN Support may have an Individual Education Plan (IEP) which provides a clear and personalised picture of their strengths, needs and the support required to help them make progress.
Each IEP begins with a pupil-centred passport-style overview, which captures:
· Strengths and interests
· Barriers to learning and participation
Individual SMART short-term targets are then identified to provide achievable steps towards the child’s longer-term goals. For each target, the IEP clearly sets out:
· Resources, provision and universal strategies
· Adaptations to teaching or the environment
· Who will provide the support and how frequently or for how long
· How progress and achievement will be evaluated
IEPs are working documents which inform adaptive classroom practice and targeted support. Progress towards targets is monitored and reviewed regularly, allowing targets, provision and adaptations to be adjusted in response to the child’s progress and changing needs.
Pupil voice is an important part of our IEP process. Children are supported to share their views, understand what they are working towards and reflect on their own progress in an age-appropriate and accessible way.
Parents and carers are invited to contribute their views as part of the IEP review process, helping to inform ongoing support, targets and next steps.
Making our IEPs accessible to children
Children receive child-friendly versions of their individual targets, helping them to understand what they are working towards, revisit their targets during learning and recognise their own progress.
Interventions and Additional Support
At St Aidan’s, some children may benefit from additional targeted support alongside high-quality, adaptive classroom teaching. Interventions are selected according to the individual needs of the child and are designed to address identified barriers to learning or development.
Targeted support may focus on areas including:
· Communication and interaction
· Cognition and learning
· Social, emotional and mental health
· Sensory and/or physical development
· Early literacy and numeracy
Examples of targeted interventions available within our school include Language Link, IDL Literacy, Sensory Circuits, SEND PE intervention, ELSA (Emotional Literacy Support) and specific speech and language interventions such as Bucket Time.
Interventions are delivered by appropriately trained staff and are monitored and reviewed to evaluate their impact. Assessment and progress information is used to determine whether support should continue, be adapted or whether an alternative approach is required. Where applicable, advice from external professionals is used to inform the support and provision provided.
Where appropriate, we aim to minimise disruption to learning and the amount of curriculum time children spend outside the classroom. Interventions are carefully planned and timetabled to balance targeted support with children’s access to high-quality teaching and the wider curriculum.
Targeted interventions complement, rather than replace, inclusive classroom teaching and children’s access to the wider curriculum.
Education, Health and Care Plans (EHCPs)
Most children with SEND have their needs supported through the school’s graduated approach and SEN Support. For some children with more complex and/or significant needs, an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) may be required.
An EHCP is a statutory plan which identifies a child’s education, health and care needs, their longer-term outcomes and the provision required to support them.
Where appropriate, St Aidan’s works closely with families and relevant professionals when considering whether an Education, Health and Care needs assessment may be required.
For children with an EHCP, we ensure that the provision outlined within the plan is implemented and that progress towards identified outcomes is regularly monitored.
EHCPs are formally reviewed through the Annual Review process. This brings together the child, their family, school and relevant professionals to celebrate progress, review needs and outcomes, and consider whether changes to the plan may be required.
Pupil voice is an important part of the Annual Review process. Children are supported to contribute in a way that is meaningful, accessible and appropriate to their individual needs and communication.
Working with External Professionals
At St Aidan’s, we recognise that some children may benefit from the advice or involvement of external professionals and specialist services. Where appropriate, we work collaboratively with families and other professionals to further understand a child’s needs and inform the support and provision provided in school.
Depending on the individual needs of the child, we may work with services and professionals including:
· Speech and Language Therapy (SALT)
· Educational Psychology
· Occupational Therapy (OT)
· SEND Advisory Team (SENDAT)
· School Nursing and other health professionals
· Local Authority SEND and specialist services
· Early Help and family support services, where appropriate
Advice and recommendations from external professionals are used, where appropriate, to inform IEPs, classroom adaptations, targeted interventions and wider provision. We work with families throughout this process and review how recommendations are supporting the child.
Independent Support for Families
Families can access free, confidential and impartial information, advice and support through RIASS (Redbridge Information, Advice and Support Service). RIASS supports children and young people with SEND and their parents and carers with information and advice about SEND, including SEN Support and Education, Health and Care Plans.
Further information can be found on the RIASS website.
https://redbridgeiass.org.uk/
Noah's Ark - Inclusive SEND Classroom
St Aidan's provides a bespoke learning classroom for children with high level special educational needs enabling children to thrive in a safe environment to meet individual needs. Specialised interventions and therapies are provided in Noah's Ark with an ambitious curriculum to enable the children to reach their full potential. The classroom is a sensory based environment immersing the children in a wide range of resources and strategies to support physical, mental, emotional and social needs.
Our children are integrated and included in the main school wherever it suits individual need and especially at lunchtime where all children participate in OPAL (Outdoor play and learning). Bespoke sport lessons are provided by trained coaches to enable the children to build their physical skills as well as focus and attention.
Outside agencies work alongside staff to support them with specialised interventions such as SALT, OT, SENDATs, School nurse.
